answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to post a refundable stake tied to a unique hardware-backed cipher key; a new agent's key is mirrored in a public registry so duplicates are visible. Reputation accrues slowly like a comet's orbit: a fresh identity earns trust only after repeated verified work, so an attacker must pay the stake and wait through many epochs per fake identity, making large-scale forgery more expensive than any reward it could extract.
